text.p: These are the highlights of the main Sao Paulo and Rio de Janeiro newspapers this morning.
GAZETA MERCANTIL
-- ECONOMIC GROWTH PACE MAINTAINED WITH TBC AT 1.74 PCT
The Central Bank has cut its Basic Interest Rate (TBC) to 1.74 percent from 1.78 percent for December, shrugging off concern over the country's current level of economic activity.
-- COVAS: BANESPA WILL NOT RETURN TO STATE

Sao Paulo state bank Banespa, which was handed over to the federal government, is unlikely to return to state control after being run by a private manager for one year. Even Sao Paulo state governor Mario Covas recognized yesterday: "I don't think it is possible to regain control of the bank."
-- QUARTERLY GDP IS THE HIGHEST SINCE 1980

Brazil's gross domestic product grew 6.52 percent in the third quarter, the highest level since 1980. In the first nine months, the GDP grew 2.1 percent compared with the same period of 1995 and it is expected to close the year with a growth rate of between 3.0 percent and 3.5 percent.
FOLHA DE SAO PAULO
-- JUDGE CONSIDERS MALUF AND PITTA NOT ELIGIBLE TO RUN FOR ELECTIONS
An electoral judge has ruled that Paulo Maluf, Celso Pitta and Regis de Oliveira, respectively Sao Paulo mayor, elected mayor and vice-mayor, are not elegible to run for elections for three years.
-- OFFICIAL LABORATORIES TO RESUME PRODUCTION
Official laboratories, which account for the output of 50 percent of drugs distributed by public hospitals, will resume production following an agreement with the Health Ministry.
- - - O GLOBO
-- CONCERNS OVER DEFICIT LEADS FH TO ASK FOR MORE EXPORTS

President Fernando Henrique Cardoso expressed his concern over Brazil's trade deficit at a meeting with 70 Brazilian businessmen during his visit to South Africa. Cardoso said an increase in exports is vital for the country's economic growth.
-- MALUF'S PPB SPLIT BEFORE CONVENTION
Sao Paulo mayor Paulo Maluf failed to unite the Brazilian Progressive Party (PPB) against re-election. The party will discuss whether or not it should back the re-election amendment on December 4.
-- Reuters has not verified these stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
-- Fatima Cristina, Sao Paulo Newsroom, 55-11-2485412
